text:
deploy-bot: Deploy started: team/runtime v2.8.1 -> production (canary 10%) at 10:23Z. CI job #4821.
incident-bot: Alert: p99 latency > 2.5s (x3 baseline) and 5xx rate 4.7% in prod.canary (detected 10:25Z). See alerts: https://telemetry.internal/recent/4821
oncall-amy: seeing the same in Grafana. p95 p99 both spiking. Canary only but trend looks bad.
eng-runtime-lead: quick check — did we change any connection pooling or kv-cache behavior in this roll? Release notes show async warmup flag toggled.
sre-jordan: rolling traces show many connections in `TIME_WAIT` and `connection_pool.acquire` latencies up. Could be connection churn during warmup. 5xxs are mostly 502/gateway timeouts.
oncall-amy: can someone grep logs for `kvcache.warmup` and `pool.acquire` around 10:24-10:26?
eng-runtime-lead: on it. snippet: ```
# query logs
jq '.ts,.level,.msg' /var/log/runtime/containers/* | grep warmup | tail -n 50
```
eng-runtime-lead: found repeated: `kvcache.warmup: started shard=3` and then `kvcache.warmup: timeout waiting for backend` — looks like warmup timeouts cascade into request stalls.
prod-support: already seeing ~14 customer-facing errors in Intercom referencing "requests timing out" since 10:26. Customers mostly low-traffic test accounts so far.
product-ops: we need a short comms note if this expands. @prod-support how many orgs impacted and severity?
prod-support: majority are dev/test; 3 paying customers have spikey errors but not full outage. Pulling session IDs now.
oncall-amy: given the pattern, I'd vote for immediate rollback of the canary to previous runtime. Can we do fast rollback?
sre-jordan: +1. Canary only currently but p99 trending upward fast; rollback preserves safety and buys time for triage.
eng-runtime-lead: agree. Initiating rollback to v2.8.0 canary at 10:29Z. Command: ```
# rollback
deploymentctl set-image runtime:production runtime:v2.8.0 --selector=canary --force
```
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by eng-runtime-lead at 10:29Z, job #4821-rollback. Canary scale 10% -> 0% for v2.8.1, 10% -> 100% for v2.8.0 (canary-target).
incident-bot: Noted: rollback start. Monitoring for p95/p99 and 5xx.
oncall-amy: monitoring metrics... p99 falling from 2.6s -> 0.7s within two minutes. p95 back to baseline. 5xx rate dropping toward 0.4%.
sre-jordan: traces after rollback show `connection_pool.acquire` latencies restored and no more warmup timeouts. Looks strongly correlated.
eng-runtime-lead: good. I'll open an issue to revert the async warmup flag flip and run a controlled test in staging with longer warmup windows.
product-ops: draft for internal ops: "Canary rolled back due to warmup-induced timeout regressions causing p99 spikes and gateway 502s. No broad customer outage; a few paying customers saw transient errors. Rollback completed at 10:31Z."
prod-support: sending short proactive notes to the 3 affected customers now, cc'ing account owners.
oncall-amy: handoff to eng-runtime for postmortem and follow-up. SRE, please keep monitoring for 30m. I'll remain on-call for the next hour.
sre-jordan: monitoring dashboards look stable. Will alert if any regressions.
eng-runtime-lead: next steps: (1) reproduce in canary with verbose kvcache logs, (2) test increased warmup timeout and connection pool backpressure, (3) add telemetry to detect warmup-induced backpressure earlier.
product-ops: assigning postmortem owner: eng-runtime-lead. ETA for draft: EOD.
oncall-amy: +1 on ownership. Thanks everyone for quick response. :raised_hands:
deploy-bot: Note: rollback job completed at 10:31:12Z.
incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated) at 10:32Z — category: deploy-induced timeout regression; severity: P2; follow-up required.
eng-runtime-lead: filing follow-up ticket: "warmup-flag-regression -> investigate pool churn" with traces attached.
prod-support: nothing new from customers in the last 10m. Closing customer-impact channel.
product-ops: will coordinate external release-notes only if follow-up finds wider risk. For now, internal summary will be posted to #postmortems.
oncall-amy: handoff: eng-runtime owns postmortem; SRE owns monitoring improvements; prod-support will update impacted customers if anything else surfaces.
eng-runtime-lead: ack. Will keep thread updated with root-cause analysis.`
